q: How does chat work in Qortal GO?
a: Q-Chat in GO, like in Hub 3.0, runs over Reticulum, a peer-to-peer network: messages go from device to device instead of through a server or the blockchain. Every message is signed with your Qortal account, and group membership comes from the Qortal chain. Your phone keeps its own chat database and fetches missed messages from other members' devices. Messages are not blockchain transactions, so sending one costs no QORT.

q: Do Q-App notifications work on the public node in GO?
aliases: do notifications need my own node
a: Yes. Q-App notifications come from the node each device is connected to, so the public node works as well as your own. Chat mentions and DMs arrive over Reticulum instead.

q: Can a Q-App see which notifications I read in other apps?
a: No. A Q-App only sees and marks its own notifications as read. It cannot learn which notifications of other Q-Apps you have read, and marking its own does not touch theirs.

q: What does "Syncing in the background" mean in GO's notification?
a: GO's background sync is keeping chat running while GO is not on the screen, because the phone is charging or you chose Always. New messages arrive and yours go out without opening GO. When the phone stops it, the notification says Chat paused instead.

q: Why did a group open in a channel other than General?
aliases: why did group open this channel
a: A group opens in the channel where you last left an unsent draft, so the draft is found where you started it. A tapped notification or a share into the group opens the channel it belongs to. Without either, the group opens in its default channel.

q: What do Join, Apply, Pending and Joined on a group invite mean?
a: On an invite card in chat, Join adds you to an open group and Apply asks to join a closed group, where an admin must accept you. Pending means your request or join is waiting for the blockchain or for an admin. Joined means you are already a member.

q: Why does a DM show Unhide user in its header?
a: You hid that person. Their messages stay out of your view until you tap Unhide user, or until the time you picked (1 hour or 24 hours) runs out.

q: Does the person know when I hide them in GO chat?
a: No. Hiding only changes what your own device shows, and it is set separately for each group and each DM. Nothing is sent to the other person, and your other devices, such as your Hub, keep showing them unless you hide them there too.

q: Why does my screen go dark during a GO call?
aliases: screen off at ear go call
a: While a 1:1 call plays through the earpiece, GO uses the phone's proximity sensor: the screen turns off when you hold the phone to your ear, so your cheek cannot press buttons, and it comes back when you move the phone away. On the speaker or a headset the screen stays on.
